Hello,大家好，我是小俊，我是腾讯新闻的科技主笔，同时也是播客节目《张小俊商业访谈录》的制作人。今天呢，坐在我对面的是奔驰汽车的全球CEO康林松先生，Mr. Ola Koenig。他1969年出生，1993年加入了奔驰汽车，在2019年担任了奔驰的全球CEO，至今已经六年了。我今天特别想跟他探讨的话题是，奔驰作为汽车发明者，在当下这个电动化、智能化转型的过程中，奔驰如何转身呢？我特别想给大家呈现的是一个转折中的一百三十九岁巨人。Hi, Mr. Ola Kalinias, I'm looking forward to our conversation today. Okay, Veneta.Fire away. So can I say that as of today, the 139 year old Mercedes-Benz is at an unprecedented turning point in its history? I think the whole auto industry is at a turning point, and we have only seen the first chapter of the fundamental transformation. This is one in a hundred years transformation. I think there are two mega trends, of course. We're on the way towards zero emission. That is the road. New energy vehicles, EVs.So zero emission is coming step by step. China is a leading market in terms of NEVs, but across the world at different speeds. Obviously, the journey is towards zero emission. The other thing is the intelligent side and AI. So I'm very excited that we're launching our new brand new CLA, the long wheelbase CLA. We have packaged literally supercomputers inside this car. One of those chips can do more than 270.Trillion calculations, it's just crazy, the amount of compute power that you have. That's what the revolution is all about. I think it, I always thought it's the most exciting industry in the world, and I have never, never worked in a period that is more exciting than what we're seeing right now. Okay, so next, let us look at into the Chinese market. Okay. Over the past six years.What has been your most important insight about this market? First of all, it's speed. There is the expression "China speed." In China, nobody waits for anybody. It's go, go, go, go, go. So the Chinese market is moving fast, but it's also innovative, especially in the digital space, automated driving, smart cockpit, language understanding. So for us, it's also crucial to work together with the leading tech companies, Tencent being one of them, obviously, and.Work with these tech companies to integrate tech that Chinese customers want, that they're used to, maybe from their smartphone, also into the vehicle. So speed and tech, I think, are the two things that that have impressed me most. Most. But as I know, Mercedes' market share in China has been dropping for the past three years, and pure electric vehicle sales have not met expectations. What do you think the reason is? And do you think this trend will continue? We're selling.Twenty years of producing Mercedes in China, we started just with a few thousand vehicles. Twenty years ago, we could never imagine that we would sell several hundred thousands of vehicles. So we worked ourselves up to a position where we were somewhere between six and seven hundred thousand vehicles. And last year we were also in the six eighty ish, which is very good. So in spite of an extremely competitive market, some pieces of the market that has also been signified by.Price wars, and new entrants, and the volume makers kind of going at each other. We have tried to, to the best of our ability, to stay out of that a little bit. You know, if you buy a Mercedes, it's not something you just buy and then you throw it away after three years. It has more value than that. So we feel that we have a strong position, but we want to kind of stay out a little bit of the price war and maybe protect the residuals for our customers than to punch the last sales figure.According to the China Automobile Dealer Association, the CADA, China's electric vehicle penetration was 4.7% in 2019, and by 2024 it had grown to whopping 47.6%. Has Mercedes lost the battle in China for electric vehicles? Absolutely not. If you look at how the trend has transpired in China, electrification has come from the bottom and gone up. So it started mostly in the entry.Segment as kind of city cars, and now are going into the volume segment. If you look at the top segment where we are dominant with the S-Class and these types of vehicles, the electric vehicles that we have, even if it's a smaller percentage of the total, we usually have the highest market share even in those even in those segments. But that's not going to be enough. We need to comprehensively expand our portfolio. The biggest segments for us in our portfolio where we think that.Most of the action is going to be where Mercedes starts. It's kind of the SUVs in our entry, like a GLB or a GLC in our core segment, C-Class, this CLA, then maybe into the E-Class and so on. And I think the best example is the latest E-Class that we launched here in China last year, long wheelbase E-Class. It's dominating that segment, and the customers love it. That is the best for you for now. You can get that from.Mercedes, but you will see a very, very, very comprehensive electric product offensive from Mercedes here in the next years. We're going to launch more cars in the next three years than we have ever launched in the history of the company. Most of them EVs. Make sure that our customers are going to have a full electric lineup at the latest in all relevant segments and models by the end of this decade. So I think these next five years are going to be crucially important for us.To build that electric market share. But in October 2020, Mercedes announced a shift in focus towards the luxury car market. I think you put more emphasis on the luxury strategy rather than electrification transition. Is that right? No, that's not right because electrification is going to happen from top to bottom. We're working on a brand new electric architecture for our performance vehicles at AMG.We have just launched an electric G-Class. I mean, the crazy go-anywhere adventure car is also now electric. So whether you're at the top of the portfolio or the entry part of the portfolio, electrification and the quest towards zero emission goes through the whole portfolio. And yes, we are in that top-end segment. We are the largest manufacturer on a worldwide basis. So it's natural for us to want to grow that segment. And it's also from a business perspective.Point of view, a profitable segment, and of course we generate the cash flow. We are we are our own venture capitalist. Yes. So the cash that we make, financial strength equals innovation strength. We put those billions back into technology and new products. But it doesn't mean that we are going to exit what we call the core segments, where you have the C class, the E class, the GLC, the GLE. So for a Chinese customer, the Mercedes portfolio as you.Know it stays roughly the same, but gets a massive, massive technological upgrade. And of course, we want to be class leading on that. I'm curious, do you like big refrigerator, widescreen TV, big sofa approach of Chinese brand car? We have here also, and in many of our cars now, what we call a super screen, so a screen that goes from pillar to pillar that feels like.It is a high-class living room, maybe with designer Italian furniture. You know what does it feel like? Welcome home feeling when you step into the car. It's maybe the most efficient car in the market now, but at the same time, I'm 195 tall. I can sit comfortably in that car. This is an entry-level Mercedes. If I sit in an S-Class, of course, I feel like a king and I have all the space. So to work on space economy, I think is right.And it's that blend that we're trying to offer to the Mercedes customers and fans around the world. Do you think the success of Fiat in the Chinese market will decide whether the global transformation of Mercedes succeeds? I think the Chinese market at the moment is the one with the fastest pace and the highest competitive pressure. So if you can be successful in the Chinese market, the likelihood that you're going to be successful in markets around the world is higher. It is the.Biggest market is our biggest market, so it is very important, and that's why we pay so much attention to it. That is why we have decided here for our next generation products to invest 14 billion RMB. This is really the place to be. Regarding the current situation, what innovative strategies do you have to turn things around in Chinese market? So building our R&D footprint, we started many many years ago an R&D.
